root.name: Queen's Gambit Declined: Hastings Variation
root.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 c6 3. Nf3 Nf6 4. Nc3 e6 5. Bg5 h6 6. Bxf6 Qxf6 7. Qb3

overview: In this Moscow Semi-Slav line White has taken on f6 and played 7.Qb3, hitting b7 and the d5 pawn. Black can defend with ...Qd8 or ...Nd7, with the bishop pair, and aims for ...dxc4 and ...b5. White gets pressure on the queenside but Black's position is resilient.

white_ideas.idea: Pressure b7 and d5 with the queen and Rb1 ideas
Develop with e3, Bd3 or Be2 and O-O

black_ideas.idea: Support b7 with ...Qd8 or ...Qb6 and develop ...Nd7, ...Bd6

typical_structures.structure: Semi-Slav structure with c6/d5/e6 against c4/d4

character.notes: Moscow Semi-Slav structure is robust, with a slow fight for queenside control.

gambit.notes: b7 is attacked but can be defended, so no gambit.

structure.notes: Centre in tension, undecided between d5 and c4.

character.reason: Black holds a solid Semi-Slav centre with the bishop pair.

gambit.reason: Pawn b7 can be defended; nothing is given.

level.reason: Both plans and some theory are needed.

plans.reason: White gave a bishop for a knight so Black has the bishop pair.
